subject: Service disruption: Atlas Health — unexpected request clipping and 429s
messages:
From: Atlas Health Ops <ops@atlashealth.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 9 Nov 2028 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: High latency + 429s since 08:50 PT — urgent

Hi Rishi,

We’re seeing a sudden spike in 429s and token-latency for our production workload starting ~08:50 PT. Error rate jumped from ~0.3% to ~6% and median token latency increased from 70ms to 380ms. This is impacting our telemedicine flow where response times matter.

We’ve attached server-side logs (debug_logs.txt) and a short SLO impact CSV. Can you confirm if this is a config change on your side? Our engineers didn’t change anything on our end.

We need an estimated recovery timeline — our on-call is already paging execs.

Thanks,
Alex Chen
Ops Lead, Atlas Health
Attachments: debug_logs.txt (text/plain), slo-impact-table.csv (text/csv)
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 9 Nov 2028 09:34:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: High latency + 429s since 08:50 PT — Atlas Health (customer P1)

Monica / Sean — forwarding Atlas’ report. They’re seeing a sharp increase in 429s + token latency. I pulled the initial traces: requests are being routed to our tiered routing fallback more frequently and a number of their tokens are being clipped by an enforcement that appears tied to a burst-window interaction with the dedicated pool.

Quick notes from my first pass: 1) Dedicated pool for Atlas was auto-fallbacking to a lower-capacity variant after a short sustained burst; 2) the burst-credit replenishment window appears shorter than intended (10s vs expected 60s) for this tenant; 3) client-side retry storms are amplifying backpressure.

Can we get Eng (runtime) on a quick triage? Monica, can you join the call with Atlas? Sean, I’ll need a one-line summary for the account slack and a copy of the contract’s burst SLA. Marissa — looping in since this is a high-impact customer and they’re already escalating to procurement.

I’ve attached the logs they sent.

— Rishi
Attachments: debug_logs.txt
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 9 Nov 2028 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: High latency + 429s since 08:50 PT — Atlas Health (customer P1)

I’m on the bridge with Atlas (joining now). They confirmed they started a small promo burst at 08:45 PT (short, predictable spike) and immediately saw degraded responses. I’ve asked their lead engineer to hold traffic steady.

On call we saw two things: 1) traffic was routed to a quantized, lower-memory variant when their dedicated nodes briefly reported a GPU OOM; 2) when routing switched, our burst-window policy dropped them below the safety threshold because replenishment was gated by the per-tenant credit loop which is currently configured to 10s. That short window is starving short-lived bursts and causes systematic clipping plus client retries that exacerbate the problem.

Requesting engineering prioritize: a) revert the replenishment tuning for affected tenant groups to 60s for the next hour; b) add a short-term override to prevent automatic routing to the low-capacity variant while we stabilize; c) enable a temporary higher burst cap for Atlas to drain queued items.

Customer impact: currently ~12% failed requests for the telemedicine flow, which crosses their SLA and is causing procurement to file a formal notice.

Monica
Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 9 Nov 2028 11:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: High latency + 429s since 08:50 PT — Atlas Health (customer P1)

Thanks for the quick triage — Monica / Rishi. I want this prioritized: Atlas is a strategic customer (top-10 ARR) and procurement is already escalating. Do the minimum safe changes to remove immediate customer pain (revert replenish window to 60s, prevent fallback to low-capacity variant, temporary burst cap increase).

Operational asks for Eng runtime: 1) implement the replenish-window override and the routing hold; 2) surface precise per-tenant metrics for the next 3 hours to my group; 3) post a short incident note in INF-1723 with the RCA sketch and timeline.

We should also prepare a customer communication: acknowledge the issue, outline immediate mitigations and an ETA for full root cause (48 hours). I’ll sign off on any small credit if needed; keep me posted if they ask for more.

Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Atlas Health Ops <ops@atlashealth.com>, procurement@atlashealth.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 9 Nov 2028 15:42:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: High latency + 429s since 08:50 PT — Atlas Health (customer P1)

Alex / Atlas team — quick update from our side and next steps:

What happened (short): a burst-window replenishment parameter was unintentionally set to 10s for your tenant cohort during an automated tuning rollout last night. That shorter replenishment period prevents small bursts from re-qualifying for burst credits and caused rapid routing into a lower-capacity variant; the routing switch + client retries produced the spike in 429s and higher token latency.

Immediate actions taken (minutes):
- Reverted replenish-window to 60s for Atlas’ tenant group (applied 10:50 PT).
- Disabled automatic fallback to the low-memory variant for Atlas while we monitor (applied 10:52 PT).
- Temporarily increased burst cap by 2x to drain the queued requests.
- Engineering enabled enhanced per-tenant telemetry and created INF-1723 for the incident notes/metrics.

Observed effect: error rate dropped from peak ~12% to ~1.1% within 20 minutes; median token latency back to ~95ms. We will keep monitoring for 3 hours.

Next steps (48h):
- Runtime team will run a postmortem and prepare a root cause memo describing why the auto-tune rollout did not include a canary for replenishment window changes.
- We will propose a change to rollout gating (safety canary + heuristics) and share a draft within 24 hours.
- If Atlas prefers, we will schedule a short call with runtime engineers to walk the patch and the timeline.

We’re very sorry for the disruption. Monica will coordinate the customer comms and I’ll follow up with the formal postmortem and any credit proposal.

— Rishi Malhotra
Account Exec — Redwood Inference
Attachments: rate_config_snapshot.json (application/json)
